// Room: P1 east flat (interior designer's part): the mirror of the west flat, one family's room on the chimney side.
// Focal piece: the lit smoker on the chimney wall (x19 z12), with the table and its chair in front of it. The bed sits
// at the back wall (x21 z14..15, head to the south wall); the barrels stand by the door. The x20 column stays clear as
// the lane from the door (x20 z9) to the bed. Light: a candle on the barrel, the lit smoker, a lantern on the table post.
import { layers, bed } from "/Volumes/ext1/swe/repos/minecraft-design/tools/src/build.mjs";

// Floor cells x19..21, z10..15 (origin 19,3,10). Layers: y3 (floor) and y4 (candle and table lantern).
const LEGEND = {
  B: ["barrel", { facing: "up" }],
  S: ["smoker", { facing: "east", lit: "true" }],
  T: ["spruce_fence"],
  l: ["lantern", { hanging: "false" }],
  C: ["spruce_stairs", { facing: "south", half: "bottom", shape: "straight" }],
  t: ["candle", { candles: "2", lit: "true" }],
};

const ROWS = [
  [
    "B.B", // z10: barrels at x19 (dresser) and x21, the lane x20 clear
    "...", // z11
    "S..", // z12: smoker at x19, on the chimney face
    "...", // z13
    "T..", // z14: table post
    "C..", // z15: chair, back to the south wall
  ],
  [
    "t..", // z10: candle on the barrel top
    "...",
    "...",
    "...",
    "l..", // z14: lantern standing on the table post (the table's lamp)
    "...",
  ],
];

export function build(g) {
  layers(g, [19, 3, 10], LEGEND, ROWS);
  bed(g, [21, 3, 14], "south", "red");
}
MAKE_OK

// Focal piece: the lit smoker on the chimney wall (x19 z12), with the table and its chair in front of it. The bed sits
// at the back wall (x21 z14..15, head to the south wall); the barrels stand by the door. The x20 column stays clear as
// the lane from the door (x20 z9) to the bed. Light: a candle on the barrel, the lit smoker, a lantern on the table post.
import { layers, bed } from "/Volumes/ext1/swe/repos/minecraft-design/tools/src/build.mjs";

// Floor cells x19..21, z10..15 (origin 19,3,10). Layers: y3 (floor) and y4 (candle and table lantern).
const LEGEND = {
  B: ["barrel", { facing: "up" }],
  S: ["smoker", { facing: "east", lit: "true" }],
  T: ["spruce_fence"],
  l: ["lantern", { hanging: "false" }],
  C: ["spruce_stairs", { facing: "south", half: "bottom", shape: "straight" }],
  t: ["candle", { candles: "2", lit: "true" }],
};

const ROWS = [
  [
    "B.B", // z10: barrels at x19 (dresser) and x21, the lane x20 clear
    "...", // z11
    "S..", // z12: smoker at x19, on the chimney face
    "...", // z13
    "T..", // z14: table post
    "C..", // z15: chair, back to the south wall
  ],
  [
    "t..", // z10: candle on the barrel top
    "...",
    "...",
    "...",
    "l..", // z14: lantern standing on the table post (the table's lamp)
    "...",
  ],
];

export function build(g) {
  layers(g, [19, 3, 10], LEGEND, ROWS);
  bed(g, [21, 3, 14], "south", "red");
}

input.summary:
P1 east flat furnished in parts/room-4.mjs: lit smoker on the chimney wall (19,3,12) as the focal stove, a fence-post table with a standing lantern and a spruce-stairs chair, two barrels (one with a lit candle), and a red bed at x21 z14..15 with its head to the back wall; the x20 column is kept clear as the lane.
Built by make.sh with no refused writes and nothing off-palette (9 blocks placed plus the bed). The room tool shows 0 dark cells (min light 10), 11/11 floor cells reachable from the inside door cell, and FIT OK.
The room is NOT walkable from the real entrance [89,1,5] in this stub copy: the door, lane and hearths are not built here. The check reads NEEDS WORK until Fittings and Lane are merged.
left: Walk from the real entrance (rooms.json [89,1,5]) reports 0 of 11 reachable only because the front door at (20,9), the step and the lane are not built in this copy; from the inside door cell (20,6,10 in file coords) all 11 cells are reachable. Recheck after the merge.

Stove cell (19,3,12) is also the Hearths part's RESERVED stove (elements #18). Hearths runs before the rooms, so if it places its own stove there my smoker write is refused and their stove stands; the room still reads, but the light and focal piece then come from their block.
plan.md's checklist has only P1-P6, so there is no room entry to tick; no elements.md item was ticked. The bed (#19) and table (#20) are built here in the room; the stove (#18) is the Hearths part's.

Rooms-check floor label says 'floor y=6' and the room box is in plan coordinates while check/walk use file y (plan y + 3): I had to read both to place the lantern and the entrance. The lantern at y6 (plan) was dropped because nothing above it exists until the roof part runs.

waste.what: Drew the room's furniture as four hand-written y-layers and worked out each cell's x/z offset by reading the plan grid; then edited the Python-style replace to swap the hanging lantern for a standing one
waste.cost: about 3 edit cycles and one full make.sh each time; roughly 10 cells placed by hand through the layers legend
waste.tool: A room-furnish helper that takes a list of [x,z,block,state] from the plan grid (or a layers() variant that accepts the plan's own 'o'/'.' grid directly) would have removed the hand-offset work.

waste.what: Walk test: the room tool's walk needs a reachable entrance, so I wrote a scratch rooms file in /tmp with the entrance at the inside door cell to see whether the furniture cut the room off
waste.cost: 3 room runs, one wrong y (plan y instead of file y); about 2 minutes
waste.tool: mcd room --entrance x,y,z (or a per-room door entrance taken from rooms.json's door list) so each room can be walk-tested from its own door without a scratch file.

waste.what: Lantern placement: could not know whether the room has a block above for a hanging lantern until the roof part exists, so I moved it to stand on the table post
waste.tool: mcd room should report 'lamp hanging needs a roof above, not yet built' separately from real dark cells, or the rooms' lantern spot planner should assume the roof will cover the box.

companions.task: Build the table as a proper joined piece (post, rail and top) and the chair seat, rather than fence-and-lantern shorthand, once the lane and furniture scale are agreed.
Once the roof part is merged, decide whether the candle on the barrel and a hanging lantern from the truss should replace the table lantern, so the room's light sits over the focal stove.
